findings.F1: The result points the way the idea predicts but is too small for this data to show it: 1,817 cases, mean excess 5-day return +0.31 % with t 1.20, a strength of 0.025 of the coin's usual 5-day move (10.60 %), about half the 0.05 that real ideas usually show (findings F10).
findings.F2: The effect is a few large gains over many small losses: the median excess return is −0.96 % and only 45 % of cases end above the coin's drift.
findings.F3: The effect is mixed across the data. By coin, ZEC carries most of it (+1.52 %, t 1.74), BTC (+0.37 %) and XRP (+0.34 %) are small, and ETH, LTC and XMR are slightly negative (−0.06 % to −0.12 %). By year, 2020 (+1.31 %, t 2.11) and 2024 (+1.49 %, t 2.05) are positive while 2022 (−1.85 %, t −2.86) and 2018 (−1.45 %) are negative. By window, the mean runs from −3.96 % (w18) to +7.33 % (w11, t 3.64).
findings.F4: The effect shows mostly when the coin was already rising before the break. Cases in the top quarter of the prior 20-day return (median +25 %) gain +1.72 % over 5 days (t 2.53, 369 cases), against −0.44 % in the bottom quarter. The same top quarter gives +1.71 % over 3 days (t 3.22) and +3.08 % over 10 days (t 2.72). Measured on the prior 10-day return, the top quarter gains +2.30 % (t 3.19).
findings.F5: Inside that rising half, the level's strength grades the move as the idea says: cases above the median of N × margin gain +1.91 % (t 2.74, 365 cases) against +0.51 % below it. Over all cases, the raw-value quintiles are not monotone (+0.19 %, −0.63 %, +1.15 %, +0.03 %, +0.84 %).
findings.F6: The prior-rise effect is not steady. Its overall Spearman correlation with the 5-day excess return is only 0.04. Only 54 % of windows have a positive mean in the rising half, against 46 % in the falling half. In 2022 both halves lose (−1.47 % and −1.51 %).
findings.F7: The idea is large enough to pay its costs: per case, the total move (+0.90 %) is 4.7 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip, and the unusual move alone is 1.6 times it. The book beats holding on Sharpe (0.74, 0.19 above holding's) but fails on its falls (Calmar 0.49).
findings.F8: Among the horizons, the 3-day one shows the effect most clearly: +0.37 % with t 1.81, against t 1.20 at 5 days and t 0.75 at 10 days. At 1 day the excess return is about zero (−0.03 %).

ideas.name: resistance breakout, all coins
ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, and the more times the level held before, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A close through a repeatedly held level exhausts the defending orders and triggers stops in the break's direction, accelerating the move, more so the more often it held.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, and the larger its 20-day return before the break and the more times the level held, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A break through a repeatedly held level after a strong run is a reason to buy for the following days, while a break after a flat or falling month is not.
ideas.name: breakout after a run
